title: Configurable per-agent models — agent_models map in PROJECT.md + wizard question + frontmatter applier
description:
Give users a durable, editable place to control which model each agent runs on, instead of hand-editing YAML frontmatter in two parity locations.

**Where the knob lives:** PROJECT.md gains an optional `agent_models` mapping (reviewer / developer / researcher → a model alias or full model ID; valid aliases per official docs: sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, inherit, or any full model ID). PROJECT.md is already the project's single config artifact (schema'd, wizard-written, round-trippable via src/project-md.js) — so the model assignment becomes project configuration, not framework internals.

**How it applies:** a frontmatter applier (natural home: extend src/agent-generator.js, which already owns generated agent guidance) reads `agent_models` and patches the `model:` line in each agent definition's frontmatter. In the dev repo that means both .claude/agents/ and the plugin-root agents/ parity copies; in user projects, .claude/agents/. Defaults when the map is absent: current shipped values (reviewer=fable, developer=sonnet, researcher=sonnet) — applier is a no-op, nothing breaks.

**Two entry points:**
1. Init wizard: an optional intake question (with the defaults pre-filled) writes the map into PROJECT.md on fresh init.
2. Change later: the user edits the `agent_models` block in PROJECT.md and re-runs the applier via a CLI flag (e.g. `node bin/init.js --apply-models` or a dedicated tiny bin — implementer's choice, but it must NOT re-run the full wizard or touch anything except agent frontmatter).

**Safety rails:** validate values against {sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, inherit} OR a full-model-ID pattern; reject unknown agent names; the applier only rewrites the `model:` frontmatter line (or inserts it after description:) — byte-stable everywhere else; parity preserved in the dev repo.

verification_tier: tdd (frontmatter rewriting + PROJECT.md round-trip parsing is exactly the mutation/parsing logic the rubric assigns to tdd).
acceptance_criteria: PROJECT.schema.json + src/project-md.js round-trip an optional agent_models map (reviewer/developer/researcher → alias or full model ID); invalid agent names or model values are rejected with a clear error

The applier patches ONLY the model: frontmatter line of each mapped agent file (inserting after description: when absent), leaving every other byte untouched, and updates both .claude/agents/ and plugin-root agents/ in the dev repo (parity spec stays green)
Init wizard offers the optional model-assignment question with current defaults (reviewer=fable, developer=sonnet, researcher=sonnet); skipping it writes no map and the applier no-ops
A CLI entry point re-applies the map from an edited PROJECT.md without re-running the wizard and without touching any non-frontmatter content

CLAUDE.md's Per-Agent Model Assignment section updated to point at PROJECT.md as the canonical knob; dist rebuilt if bin/ or bundled src/ changed; full suite green (touches schema-adjacent parsing → test:all gate)

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: TIER ASSIGNMENT: verification_tier = tdd — PROJECT.md schema/round-trip parsing + surgical frontmatter rewriting are state-mutation/parsing logic per the rubric. GATE: scaled — NOT a test-infra ticket; developer must grep-derive the affected-e2e list (expect at minimum: project-md, project-schema, round-trip, init, intake-e2e, agent-models fast-tier, agents-parity) and run fast tier + that list; reviewer may veto. LOCKED DESIGN beyond the ticket description: (1) PROJECT.md frontmatter key `agent_models` as an inline-map-per-agent encoding consistent with existing frontmatter conventions (writer/reader live in src/project-md.js; schema in state/PROJECT.schema.json with additionalProperties:false on the map: only reviewer/developer/researcher keys). (2) Valid values: {sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, inherit} or full model ID matching /^claude-[a-z0-9-]+$/; reject unknown agents/values BEFORE any write. (3) The applier is a pure function in src/agent-generator.js (e.g. applyAgentModels({repoRoot, agentModels})) returning which files changed; bin entry = a flag on bin/init.js (--apply-models: reads PROJECT.md, applies, exits — no wizard); wizard question OPTIONAL with defaults prefilled (skipping writes no map). (4) Surgical edit guarantee: only the model: line inside the YAML frontmatter block may change (insert after description: when absent); every other byte preserved — encode as a byte-comparison test. (5) Dev-repo dual-write: when agents/ parity dir exists, applier updates both copies; user projects (no parity dir) update .claude/agents/ only.
